review_notes: I read the whole file and the supporting definitions: lowDegree and its lemmas in EdgeProducts.lean, colorAverage (a Module.End ℝ) in EdgeMonomials.lean, and Submodule.smul_mem_iff in Mathlib. Two proofs can be shortened without losing clarity. Neither replacement was compiled. The remaining proofs (colorAverage_recurrence, list_prod_mem_lowDegree, lowDegree_lift) looked reasonable as written. I did not flag them because the replacements I considered were taste-level or less clear.

findings.excerpt:
apply Submodule.span_induction (p := fun f _ => colorAverage z f ∈
    lowDegree (tableCoordinate z) d) _ _ _ _ hf
findings.problem: The proof runs a four-case Submodule.span_induction by hand. Only the generator case carries mathematical content. The zero, add and smul cases just re-prove that the preimage of a submodule under the linear map `colorAverage z` is a submodule. `colorAverage z` is a `Module.End ℝ`, so this closure is already available as `Submodule.comap`. The neighbouring `lowDegree_substitute` already proves the same kind of statement with `Submodule.span_le` and only a generator check.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the body with a span_le argument against the comap, so only the generator case remains:

  have hle : lowDegree Pairing.edgeCoord d ≤
      (lowDegree (tableCoordinate z) d).comap (colorAverage z) := by
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro f ⟨l, hl, rfl⟩
    exact lowDegree_mono _ hl (colorAverage_monomial_mem z l)
  exact hle hf

Membership in the comap is definitionally `colorAverage z f ∈ ...`, so `exact hle hf` should close the goal.
findings.benefit: The three routine closure cases and their `simpa` calls go away. The proof reads as "check on generators, then use linearity", the same shape as `lowDegree_substitute` a few lines below, so the file is more consistent and the key idea is easier to see.

findings.excerpt:
have hh := (lowDegree (tableCoordinate z) (1+l.length)).smul_mem D⁻¹ hmem
        simpa only [smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ hD, one_smul, Nat.add_comm,
          List.length_cons] using hh
findings.problem: To cancel the nonzero scalar D, the proof multiplies by D⁻¹ and then needs smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ and one_smul to undo it. Mathlib has `Submodule.smul_mem_iff`, which says that for nonzero s, `s • x ∈ p ↔ x ∈ p`, over a `DivisionSemiring` of scalars. ℝ qualifies.
findings.proposed_change:
After the existing `change ... at hmem`, finish with:

  have hh := (Submodule.smul_mem_iff _ hD).mp hmem
  simpa only [Nat.add_comm, List.length_cons] using hh

This states directly that a nonzero scalar multiple lies in the submodule iff the vector does. It drops the D⁻¹ round trip and the three algebraic simp lemmas.
findings.benefit: The "divide by the nonzero count D" step becomes a single named lemma. The reader no longer has to follow smul_smul / inv_mul_cancel₀ / one_smul to see that it is just cancelling D.
